chunks: And We opened up the flood gates of the sky with water pouring down in torrents,

key_terms.أَبْوَابَ: Gates or doors, metaphorically referring to the sources or channels of rain from the sky.
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: The sky or heaven, here indicating the upper realms from which rain descends.
key_terms.مُنْهَمِرٍ: Pouring down copiously or in torrents, describing the intensity and abundance of the rain.

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'gates of the sky' refer to in the context of the Great Flood?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qamar is often linked to the concept of divine signs (Ayat) that were rejected by the disbelievers of Noah, emphasizing the suddenness and overwhelming nature of the deluge. The phrase 'abwab' (gates) suggests distinct sources or layers of the sky, reflecting the cosmic order's responsiveness to God's command. This event serves as a precursor to the Day of Judgment, illustrating how natural elements become instruments of divine justice.
